Forbes Field named candidate for KC-46A mission, Senator Marshall responds
Senator Roger Marshall praised Forbes Field being named a candidate location for a new KC-46A Pegasus mission by the Air National Guard. The base could receive eight new aircraft if selected after upcoming town halls review all four candidates.
U.S. Senator Roger Marshall praised the Air National Guard’s decision on Oct. 1 to identify Forbes Field Air National Guard Base in Topeka as one of four candidate locations for its next KC-46A Pegasus mission.
“This is great news for Kansas and well-deserved recognition of the men and women of the 190th Air Refueling Wing,” said Senator Marshall. “Forbes Field has the infrastructure, the experience and, most importantly, the outstanding Airmen needed to take on this next-generation mission.”
The Secretary of the Air Force approved Forbes Field along with Bangor Air National Guard Base in Maine, Key Field Air National Guard Base in Mississippi, and Rickenbacker Air National Guard Base in Ohio as candidate locations for Mission Operations Base 9. The selected location is expected to receive eight KC-46A aircraft.
Brigadier General Paul Schneider said, “Forbes Field is the absolute right place for basing the KC-46A Pegasus. The Kansas Airmen of the 190th Air Refueling Wing continue to set the standard for excellence, as demonstrated by their flawless execution during Operation Epic Fury, their ability to maintain personnel strength above 100% of authorized, and remarkable maintenance record. As the Secretary of the Air Force moves forward with the MOB 9 strategic basing process, the 190th stands ready to recapitalize their legacy KC-135s with the modern capability of eight KC-46A aircraft, ensuring Kansas remains the premier hub for global reach.”
In coming weeks, town halls will be conducted at each candidate location by the Basing and Conversions Division to discuss site-survey criteria and upcoming milestones.
Marshall's office provides services such as military academy nominations, assistance with federal agencies, American flag requests, internships and tour arrangements to benefit Kansas residents; he served seven years in the U.S. Army Reserves; he grew up as a fifth-generation farm kid who was first in his family to pursue higher education; earned degrees from Butler County Community College, Kansas State University and University of Kansas School of Medicine; chairs subcommittees on conservation within agriculture as well as primary health within health committees; and participates in congressional caucuses, according to the official website.
